newsitem.title: USA: Occidental raises 1997 cap spending 13 pct.
newsitem.headline: Occidental raises 1997 cap spending 13 pct.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp Thursday said it plans to increase 1997 capital spending by 13 percent to $1.34 billion.
In a statement, Occidental said its oil and gas division will receive $900 million this year, up 18 percent, and its chemical division will receive $325 million, up 24 percent.
The capital budget for natural gas transmission and marketing this year will be set at $115 million.
Occidental said the majority of the capital allocated to its oil and gas division would go toward international operations such as the development of reserves in Qatar.

Occidental said it replaced a total of 124 percent of worldwide oil and gas production last year. Worldwide oil reserve additions were 119 million barrels, up 114 percent, and worlwide natural gas reserve additions were 392 billion cubic feet, up 150 percent.

Occidental said its finding and development costs per barrel of oil equivalent were $3.80 for international operations and $4.15 worldwide. Over the last five years, Occidental's average finding and development costs were $2.74 a barrel for international and $3.28 worldwide.
